gaps.sentence: There's still a lot of paperwork ___ (complete) before we can close the account.
gaps.explanation: Noun + passive to-infinitive (paperwork to be completed) — the paperwork receives the action.

gaps.sentence: The evidence ___ by an independent laboratory at present.
gaps.explanation: 'At present' needs present continuous passive: is being + analysed. The lab does the analysing.

gaps.sentence: The ruins ___ (discover) by farmers digging a well in 1923.
gaps.explanation: Past simple passive with a expressed agent: were discovered by farmers.

gaps.sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
gaps.explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

gaps.sentence: Several issues remain ___ (resolve) before the launch.
gaps.explanation: 'Remain' + passive infinitive (to be resolved) expresses unfinished business.

gaps.sentence: The match ___ (abandon) because of the storm, so we got a refund.
gaps.explanation: Modal passive with have to: had to be + past participle for past obligation.

gaps.sentence: The castle ___ in the twelfth century.
gaps.explanation: A completed past date takes the past simple passive.

gaps.sentence: The decision ___ (announce) at yesterday's press conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' signals past simple passive: was + announced.
